original_query: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(EXPR0), 0), T2 FROM (SELECT t5.T2, COUNT(CASE WHEN EMP1.DEPTNO = 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS EXPR0 FROM EMP AS EMP1, (VALUES (1)) AS t5 (T2) GROUP BY t5.T2 UNION ALL SELECT t8.T2, COUNT(CASE WHEN EMP2.DEPTNO = 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) AS EXPR0 FROM EMP AS EMP2, (VALUES (2)) AS t8 (T2) GROUP BY t8.T2) AS t11 GROUP BY T2
rewritten_query:
SELECT agg.cnt::numeric AS "coalesce", v.t2
FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM emp
    WHERE deptno = 0
) AS agg
CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (2)) AS v(t2)
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM emp)

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate the UNION ALL of two nearly identical branches that each scan and aggregate EMP (45M rows each). Replace with a single aggregation over EMP cross joined with the constant values (1),(2).
Remove the redundant outer GROUP BY/SUM/COALESCE: each inner branch produces at most one row per T2, so SUM over one row is a no-op and COUNT is never NULL.
Replace COUNT(CASE WHEN deptno = 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END) with a direct filtered count (COUNT(*) FROM emp WHERE deptno = 0), which is clearer and index-friendly.

Use EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM emp) as the empty-table guard instead of computing COUNT(*) over all 45M rows; EXISTS stops at the first row. This preserves the original behavior of returning no rows when EMP is empty (the original inner GROUP BY over an empty cross join yields no groups, so COALESCE never creates rows).
